creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 4. `peer` was written against v0.11.0 and shipped to a machine running v0.10.1, where it fails at load:

```
error[RAD20028]: Undefined identifier 'get_os'
  --> peer:92:10
   = help: did you mean 'get_args', 'get_env', or 'get_pid'?
```

Same for `mkdir` and `format_epoch`. The diagnostic is right-shaped for a typo and wrong-shaped for the actual cause: nothing says the interpreter predates the function. For scripts synced across machines, version skew is a normal state of the world.

`@min_version` in the file header - the `@enable_args_block` shape already exists - turns three misleading errors into one true one.

Calibration positive worth keeping: running the *old* machine's `rad check` against the script produced the complete skew report in one shot, did-you-mean hints included. That's accidentally a good cross-version workflow and could be advertised as the pre-ship check. It depends on the over-arity destructuring hole in p0-tier1 being closed.

---

### Orientation

- Header macros live in the `--- ... ---` file header, parsed into `rl.FileHeader.MetadataEntries` (a `map[string]string`, `rts/rl/ast_types.go:694-706`).
- There are already three macros, all consts in `core/consts.go`: `MACRO_ENABLE_ARGS_BLOCK` (line 15), plus `MACRO_ENABLE_GLOBAL_OPTIONS` and `MACRO_STASH_ID`. They are read in one place - `core/script_meta.go:40-47` - via `defaultTruthyMacroToggle`.
- Enforcement for `enable_args_block` happens in `core/runner.go:303`, in `registerScript`. That is the shape to copy, but not the timing (see below).
- The running version is `core.Version` at `core/version.go:4` (currently `v0.11.0`).

### Where to start

- `core/script_meta.go:40-47` - add the parse of `@min_version` here so the value lands alongside the other header-derived script metadata.
- `core/runner.go:62-92` is the phase ordering: detection and setup, then registration, then `parseAndExecute`. The version gate has to fire **before** the static checker reports undefined identifiers, otherwise the author still sees the three misleading `RAD20028`s and never reaches the true message. Trace where `rts/check` runs in `parseAndExecute` and insert ahead of it.
- Version comparison: there is no semver helper in `core/` today - check `go.mod` before adding a dependency; a small parse of `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` in `core/` is likely enough given Rad's own version format.
- New error code in `rts/rl/errors.go`, **4xxxx band** (validation/lint). Numbers are never reused - the tombstone rule keeps retired codes declared with a `_retired` suffix, so take the next free number rather than filling a gap.
- Every new code needs a user-facing doc at `core/error_docs/<code>.md`. Style guide is `core/error_docs/AGENTS.md`; `core/error_docs/40008.md` is a good model of a version-related message.

### How to verify

```sh
make build
./bin/radd script-with-min-version.rad
go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=misc/macros
go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=misc/file_header
make test
```

Existing header/macro coverage lives in `core/testing/snapshots/misc/macros.snap` and `core/testing/snapshots/misc/file_header.snap`.

### Done when

- A script declaring a `@min_version` above the running interpreter's version exits with one clear error naming both versions, instead of N undefined-identifier errors.
- A script declaring a satisfied `@min_version` runs unchanged.
- A malformed version string is its own diagnostic, not a silent pass.
- `core/error_docs/<code>.md` exists and `rad docs RAD<code>` renders it.
- `SYNTAX.md` documents the macro - it is the language reference and lists the existing macros.
- `make generate` committed (error docs feed `docs-web/docs/reference/errors.md` and `core/embedded_docs/`, both generated).

### Watch out for

`AGENTS.md` says to prefer static detection in `rts/check/` so editors surface it too - but **rts must not import core**, and `Version` lives in core. Either thread the running version into the checker as an input, or accept a runtime-only check and note why. Decide this before writing code; retrofitting is the expensive direction.

The card's dependency on the over-arity destructuring hole (p0-tier1) is about the *calibration workflow* it praises, not about this macro. `@min_version` itself is independent - do not block on it.
title: Add a @min_version header macro
